# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Loop/Path Drawing
Puzzles where the solver draws a single continuous loop or path through the grid.

#### A1. Pure Loop Construction
- **Masyu** – Loop through cells with black/white circle constraints on turning/straight behavior
- **Slitherlink** – Loop along grid edges with numeric constraints on surrounding line segments
- **Mid-loop** – Loop through cells where black circles must be midpoints of straight segments
- **Nagareru** – Directed loop with wind constraints affecting direction of travel
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop through rooms alternating between moon and sun symbols
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop through cells with per-region constraints on circle behavior (all straight or all turning)
- **Suraromu** – Loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing through all gates in specified order

#### A2. Loop with Cell Shading
- **Yajilin** – Loop construction combined with placing black cells indicated by arrow-number clues

#### A3. Path Connection
- **Numberlink** – Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing paths
- **Nurimeizu** – Create a maze path from S to G by painting walls, with circle/triangle routing constraints

### B. Cell Shading/Painting
Puzzles where the solver determines which cells to shade black (or leave white).

#### B1. Shading with Numeric Clues on Adjacency
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs that illuminate rows/columns; numbered black cells constrain adjacent bulb count
- **Kurotto** – Shade cells where circled numbers indicate sum of adjacent continuous black cell groups
- **Kurodoko** – Shade cells where numbers indicate total visible white cells in four directions
- **Usowan** – Shade cells where numbers show adjacent shaded count, but exactly one number per room is wrong

#### B2. Shading with Regional Constraints
- **Heyawake** – Shade cells in rooms with count constraints; no adjacent shaded cells; white cells connected; no white line spans 3+ rooms
- **Nurikabe** – Shade to form a connected wall; white islands each contain one number indicating island size; no 2×2 black squares
- **Nurimisaki** – Shade cells where circled cells must be white promontories; no 2×2 of either color
- **Norinori** – Shade exactly two cells per region, each shaded cell part of a domino
- **LITS** – Shade a tetromino in each region; connected shading; no 2×2 squares; no same-shaped tetrominoes touching
- **Nuritwin** – Shade cells so each region has exactly two equal-sized shaded blocks; all shading connected; no 2×2
- **Sto-stone** – Shade cells in rooms with count constraints; shaded cells don't connect across rooms; "dropped" stones fill bottom half

#### B3. Shading with Shape Constraints
- **Choco Banana** – Shade cells where black groups must form rectangles; white groups must not form rectangles; numbers indicate area size
- **Shakashaka** – Place triangles in cells so remaining white space forms rectangles/squares; numbers constrain adjacent triangle count
- **Tilepaint** – Color entire tiles (regions) so that diagonal-cell clue numbers are satisfied

#### B4. Shading by Elimination (Given Numbers)
- **Hitori** – Shade duplicate numbers so no number repeats in any row/column; no adjacent shaded cells; white cells connected

### C. Number/Symbol Placement
Puzzles where the solver fills cells with numbers or symbols.

#### C1. Number Filling with Regional Constraints
- **Sudoku** – Fill 1–9 in rows, columns, and 3×3 blocks without repetition
- **Fillomino** – Fill numbers forming blocks of size equal to the number; same-sized blocks can't touch
- **Ripple Effect** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; duplicate numbers in a line must have sufficient spacing
- **Makaro** – Fill rooms with 1 to N; arrow cells point to the largest neighbor; no equal adjacent numbers across rooms
- **Nansuke** – Place given multi-digit numbers into a crossword-style grid

#### C2. Symbol Placement
- **Juosan** – Fill every cell with — or |; territory constraints on relative counts; limits on consecutive same-orientation marks
- **Hebi** – Place numbered snake segments (1–5) with visibility and non-adjacency constraints

### D. Grid Division/Partitioning
Puzzles where the solver divides the grid into regions or blocks.

#### D1. Division into Rectangles
- **Shikaku** – Divide grid into rectangles each containing exactly one number equal to the rectangle's area

#### D2. Division into Specified Shapes
- **Five Cells** – Divide grid into pentominoes; numbers indicate surrounding block edges
- **Sashigane** – Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows mark ends pointing to bends

#### D3. Division with Matching Subregions
- **Double Choco** – Divide into blocks each containing matching white and gray areas of identical shape

#### D4. Division with Evolving Shapes
- **Evolomino** – Place square markers forming blocks along arrows, each successive block adding one square to the previous shape

#### D5. Block Identification with Chaining
- **Chained Block** – Identify black-cell blocks containing their size number; all blocks must chain via diagonal contact; no duplicate shapes in a chain

### E. Bridge/Connection Drawing
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect island circles with 1–2 bridges matching island numbers; no crossing; all islands connected

### F. Object Movement
Puzzles where the solver moves given objects to new positions.

- **Satogaeri** – Move circles within countries so each country has exactly one; numbers indicate movement distance; paths can't cross
- **Yosenabe** – Move circles straight into gray areas; numbers in gray areas equal the sum of entering circle values

---

## II. By Constraint Mechanisms (Cross-cutting)

### Connectivity Requirements
White/unshaded cells must form a connected network: **Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Usowan**
Shaded cells must be connected: **LITS, Nuritwin, Nurikabe** (black wall)
Loop must be single and continuous: **Masyu, Slitherlink, Mid-loop, Nagareru, Moon-or-Sun, Dotchi-Loop, Suraromu, Yajilin**
Bridges must connect all islands: **Hashiwokakero**

### No 2×2 Constraint
No 2×2 block of same color: **Nurikabe, LITS, Nurimisaki, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Nurimeizu**

### Non-adjacency of Shaded Cells
Shaded cells cannot touch orthogonally: **Heyawake, Hitori, Usowan, Yajilin**

### Visibility/Line-of-Sight Clues
Numbers indicate visible cells or objects along rows/columns: **Akari, Kurodoko, Nurimisaki, Yajilin, Hebi**

### Regional/Room Constraints
Grid pre-divided into rooms with per-room rules: **Heyawake, Moon-or-Sun, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Double Choco, Norinori, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Nurimeizu, Usowan, Dotchi-Loop, Suraromu, Five Cells**

### Deception/Liar Constraints
- **Usowan** – Exactly one number per room is incorrect

### Gravity/Physical Simulation
- **Sto-stone** – Stones must fill bottom half when "dropped"

### Directional Constraints
- **Nagareru** – Wind direction restricts loop movement
- **Makaro** – Arrows point to the largest adjacent number
- **Yajilin** – Arrow-number clues indicate black cells in a direction
- **Evolomino** – Arrows define growth direction of blocks
- **Hebi** – Snake head direction determines line of sight for attack rules
- **Sashigane** – Arrows point toward the bend of L-shapes
- **Pencils** – Tips define line origin and direction
